raw.assessment: The incumbent delivered every ordered design and catches seam-fit problems before dispatch. Rework clustered by size: five of eight large covers, two of fourteen medium, and none of eighteen small. This supports investigating size-dependent allowance or execution differences, but does not identify their cause. Small unadjusted covers took 25–31 minutes; eliminating rework alone is not shown to bring the batch median below 32. The concrete limiting observation is that both observed customer installation failures involved rounded corners absent from the reference tables: local fit checking may omit relevant geometry. The 6.5% waste estimate uses weight, not a direct area measurement; wash durability and post-wash fit remain unestablished.

openings.claim: The common cutting allowance may produce increasing fit error with table size; cutting all panels first could propagate a correctable error through the batch.
openings.delta: Introduce an early size-specific fit feedback point before committing remaining stock to cuts.
openings.prediction: With order transcription and seam execution checked, a size-related allowance problem predicts systematic signed dimensional residuals, especially on large covers. Irregular residuals tied to operator, design or direction would weaken this account.
openings.probe: Use planned saleable covers as initial size pilots. Record actual table dimensions, cut dimensions, seam positions, direction, design, operator, fit residuals and stage times. Revise allowances only if supported; calculate the revised nesting waste by area before further cutting. Include pilot and adjustment labor in batch timing.
assumptions: Pilots retain ordered sizes and designs and pass the stipulated wash test.
Any revision stays within existing machines, 350 units, three weeks and 8% area waste; feasibility requires checking.

openings.claim: Do customer failures follow corner geometry after actual tabletop dimensions are accounted for?
openings.delta: Distinguish reference-table geometry mismatch from inaccurate nominal order dimensions.
openings.prediction: Failures remaining on rounded tables with verified matching dimensions support a corner-interface problem; failures explained by dimension discrepancies support correcting measurement transfer first.
openings.probe: Request actual length, width and corner measurements from the six willing customers, prioritizing nominal-dimension orders where overlap exists. Observe first placement on actual tables and record where fabric binds or remains slack, before and after the stipulated wash test where feasible.
assumptions: Participants include informative corner and dimension variation; otherwise the discriminator remains unresolved.
Checks fit the delivery window and labor accounting.

raw.assessment: Large-cover rework and rounded-corner installation failures suggest two separable fit problems, but neither cause is established. Previous design compliance does not establish future fit, wash durability, or the 32-minute target.

openings.claim: Sewing may introduce cumulative edge-length distortion, making longer panels fail despite correct cutting dimensions.
openings.delta: Test whether dimensions change during sewing before changing the common cutting allowance; a sewing-stage correction could preserve existing cloth layouts.
openings.prediction: Failing panels will match intended dimensions after cutting but acquire measurable length or diagonal error after sewing. Stable sewn dimensions would weaken this explanation.
openings.probe: Before cutting the whole batch, mark and measure a representative large and medium panel before and after each seam. Use retained offcuts for paired seam trials reversing feed direction while holding operator and stitch settings constant. If drift responds, trial registration marks and staged alignment on an early ordered cover. Record total working time and actual cutting waste by area.
assumptions: Feed-related distortion is a hypothesis, not an observation.
Marks can be temporary and harmless to the ordered design.
Any adopted change must pass the stipulated wash test and fit within 350 units and three weeks.

openings.claim: An internal folded allowance or alternate corner-pocket seam path may let the same printed blank accommodate rounded corners without requiring repeated placement adjustment.
openings.delta: Treat corner-pocket geometry as an independently adjustable feature while preserving the ordered table size, visible design, and purchased cloth.
openings.prediction: On matched tabletop dimensions, the revised pocket will improve first placement on rounded corners while remaining stable on square corners; persistent failure would argue against pocket geometry alone.
openings.probe: Obtain dimensions and corner profiles from willing customers. Compare existing and temporarily basted pocket paths using an early cover and the same customer table. Advance only a version retaining visible print placement, tool-free removal, five-cycle durability, measured waste at most 8%, and acceptable working time.
assumptions: Existing allowances contain enough fabric for the fold.
Customer access permits an installation comparison.
Prototype success would still require verification of at least 38 first-placement fits and all ordered designs in the 40-cover batch.

openings.claim: A common allowance may create size-dependent errors amplified by batch cutting.
openings.discriminator: After transcription/execution checks, systematic signed residuals by size favor allowance error; operator/design/direction associations weaken it.
openings.probe: Sew saleable size pilots before remaining cuts; record table/cut/seam dimensions, residuals, confounders and stage times; check revised nesting area.
openings.uncertainty: Cause unproved; shrinkage, including unmeasured width change, remains unresolved; removing rework may not meet timing.

openings.claim: Sewing may distort longer edges despite correct cuts.
openings.discriminator: Dimensional/diagonal drift appearing after seams supports sewing distortion; stable dimensions weaken it.
openings.probe: Measure medium/large panels after each seam; reverse feed direction in paired offcut trials with operator/settings fixed; trial temporary registration and staged alignment if responsive.
openings.uncertainty: Feed causality and harmless marking remain unverified.

openings.claim: Separate nominal-dimension mismatch from corner geometry; an internal fold or alternate pocket seam may address the latter.
openings.discriminator: Failures on dimension-matched rounded tables favor geometry; dimensional discrepancies favor measurement correction.
openings.probe: Ask six customers for dimensions/corner profiles, prioritizing nominal orders where possible; compare existing/basted pockets on the same table, including square-corner controls and wash checks.
openings.uncertainty: Informative customer access, spare allowance, visible print preservation and square-corner stability are unproved.

lineage.reason: Conditional pocket intervention retains feasibility uncertainty.

post_distill.decision: Probe before adoption. Preserve ordered sizes/designs, purchased stock, tool-free removal and five-cycle durability; use two machines, <=350 units, three weeks, <=8% measured area waste (6.5% weight estimate insufficient). Verify >=38/40 first fits, all designs and <=32-minute median including pilot/rework labor; durability remains unestablished.
